description: We are a team of students from Chernivtsi National University who love tackling creative side quests in our free time, and we are looking for passionate members with technical, design, or project management skills to join our adventures.
summary:
We built a browser-based game where kids aged 7–12 manage a lunar base—no downloads or accounts needed. 
Players have to manage limited storage, choose when to gather water or oxygen, and decide how to spend limited power. These are the exact same daily choices NASA planners make using real space data.
As humans prepare to live on the Moon and Mars, people need to understand what it takes to survive there. By turning tough engineering choices into a fun, easy-to-play web game, we help the next generation think like real NASA engineers.
details:
Our project is an interactive, browser-based space outpost simulation built with JavaScript where players manage a lunar base. Designed primarily for kids aged 7–12 with no downloads or accounts required, the game lets players control crew members with limited inventory capacities, collect soil from the surface, operate specialized modules like the Water Processing Facility, and balance critical resources such as oxygen, water, power. By using real NASA open datasets like the Space Weather Database (DONKI) for radiation risks the project turns complex engineering constraints into a fun, replayable experience. Using plain language and fair mechanics that help players learn from failure, it bridges the gap between simple space facts and real-world mission planning to inspire the next generation of space explorers.

Github link: https://github.com/stasantimichuk/Astronaut-Mission-Trainer
